headlines.title: Old Dominion Freight Line (ODFL) Stock Looks Rich Against Cash Flow
headlines.summary: Old Dominion Freight Line has seen its share price move steadily higher, and that kind of climb naturally raises a question for investors who care about cash returns. After a strong stretch on the Nasdaq, the issue is whether the current market value lines up with the freight carrier's underlying cash flows. Old Dominion Freight Line has returned 34.8% over the past year, which puts more pressure on the cash flow story to explain why the stock is priced where it is today.

headlines.title: Old Dominion Freight Line Announces $0.29 Per Share Quarterly Cash Dividend
headlines.summary: THOMASVILLE, N.C., October 22, 2026--Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc. (Nasdaq: ODFL) today announced that its Board of Directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.29 per share of common stock, payable on December 16, 2026, to shareholders of record at the close of business on December 2, 2026. This dividend payment represents a 3.6% increase to the quarterly cash dividend paid in December 2025.

description: Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc. operates as a less-than-truckload motor carrier in the United States and North America. The company offers regional, inter-regional, and national less-than-truckload services, as well as expedited transportation services. It also provides various value-added services, including container drayage, truckload brokerage, and supply chain consulting. In addition, the company operates fleet maintenance centers. As of December 31, 2025, it owned and operated 10,184 tractors, 30,824 linehaul trailers, and 14,313 pickup and delivery trailers. Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc. was founded in 1934 and is headquartered in Thomasville, North Carolina.
